      "title": "Reconstruct the expected public interface from the header and build files before implementing",
      "pattern": "Before writing any implementation, read the provided header (and CMakeLists.txt) to extract the exact namespace, class/function names, signatures, and return types the hidden tests will call. When the header is a stub or ambiguous, infer the canonical Exercism interface from the exercise name and the stub's namespace, then define the header yourself to match that interface.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden tests compile against the header's declared interface. Getting names/signatures wrong causes compile failures regardless of logic correctness. Reading the header first anchors all subsequent code to the real contract.",
      "examples": [
        "read_file('zebra_puzzle.h') then read_file('CMakeLists.txt') before writing zebra_puzzle.cpp",
        "read_file('space_age.h') and CMakeLists.txt, then write space_age.h with class space_age and on_<planet>() accessors",
        "read_file('linked_list.h') to discover the List<T> template API (push/pop/shift/unshift/count/erase) before implementing"
      ],
      "scope": "Any task where a stub header defines or constrains the public API consumed by hidden tests.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Write a standalone self-test harness that exercises the public API, then compile and run it",
      "pattern": "Create a temporary main/self-test file that includes the header, calls the public API with representative and boundary inputs, and asserts expected results. Compile it together with the implementation using strict flags and run it. Iterate on the implementation until the harness passes, then delete the harness.",
      "why_it_helps": "The hidden test file is unavailable, so a self-authored harness is the only executable feedback loop. It catches signature mismatches, logic errors, and boundary bugs before submission.",
      "examples": [
        "write_file('_selftest.cpp') with asserts for clock normalization (24:00 -> 00:00, negative minutes) then g++ ... && ./_selftest",
        "write_file('selftest.cpp') asserting diamond rows for 'A','C','E' plus square/symmetry checks, then compile and run",
        "write_file('selfcheck.cpp') for linked_list covering push/pop/shift/unshift/count/erase, compiled with -fsanitize=address,undefined"
      ],
      "scope": "Any implementation task with hidden tests and a compilable language.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "title": "Use strict compiler flags to surface warnings as errors",
      "pattern": "Compile self-tests with -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror (and -pthread when threading is involved). Treat any warning as a failure to fix.",
      "why_it_helps": "Strict flags catch unused variables, sign-conversion issues, missing returns, and other latent bugs that could also break the hidden build or indicate logic errors.",
      "examples": [
        "g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -I. _selftest.cpp clock.cpp -o _selftest",
        "g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -I. selfcheck.cpp bank_account.cpp -o selfcheck"
      ],
      "scope": "C++ compilation tasks.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Redirect TMPDIR to a workspace-local directory to work around sandbox cache errors",
      "pattern": "When the compiler fails with 'couldn't create cache file ... Operation not permitted', create a local temp directory and set TMPDIR (and sometimes TMP/TEMP) to it before invoking the compiler.",
      "why_it_helps": "The sandbox blocks writes to the default system temp path, causing spurious compile failures. Redirecting TMPDIR to a writable workspace path unblocks the build without changing the code.",
      "examples": [
        "export TMPDIR=\"$PWD/.tmp\"; mkdir -p .tmp; g++ ... -o scratch_run && ./scratch_run",
        "mkdir -p _tmp && TMPDIR=\"$PWD/_tmp\" TMP=\"$PWD/_tmp\" TEMP=\"$PWD/_tmp\" g++ ... && ./_selftest",
        "mkdir -p .selftest/tmp && TMPDIR=\"$PWD/.selftest/tmp\" g++ ... && ./.selftest/selftest"
      ],
      "scope": "Sandboxed build environments where the default temp directory is not writable.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Enumerate and test boundary/edge cases explicitly in the self-test",
      "pattern": "Identify the boundary conditions implied by the problem statement (empty input, zero/negative values, overflow/wrap-around, full/empty containers, invalid input, duplicate entries) and write explicit assertions for each in the self-test harness.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden tests typically include edge cases. Explicitly testing them forces the implementation to handle them and reveals off-by-one or normalization bugs early.",
      "examples": [
        "clock self-test asserts clock(24,0)==\"00:00\", clock(0,-60)==\"23:00\", clock(-1,0)==\"23:00\"",
        "knapsack self-test asserts maximum_value(0,{{1,1}})==0, maximum_value(-5,...)==0, single item too heavy",
        "phone_number self-test asserts invalid area/exchange codes throw, and 11-digit numbers starting with 1 are accepted"
      ],
      "scope": "Any task with defined rules and boundary conditions.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Cross-check the implementation against an independent brute-force reference for combinatorial problems",
      "pattern": "For problems with a large search space (e.g., constraint puzzles), write a separate brute-force program that enumerates all possibilities and counts solutions, then compare its answer to the optimized implementation's answer.",
      "why_it_helps": "An independent reference validates correctness of the optimized logic and confirms the solution is unique, catching subtle constraint-encoding errors that self-tests based on the same logic might miss.",
      "examples": [
        "write_file('scratch_ref.cpp') brute-force counting solutions=1 and printing water/zebra, compared to the optimized zebra_puzzle.cpp output",
        "write_file('.tmp/count.cpp') enumerating permutations to verify the puzzle has exactly one solution"
      ],
      "scope": "Constraint-satisfaction or combinatorial tasks where a brute-force reference is feasible.",
      "confidence": 0.8
    },
    {
      "title": "Clean up all temporary artifacts after verification",
      "pattern": "After self-tests pass, remove scratch source files, compiled binaries, and temp directories so only the required implementation and header remain in the workspace.",
      "why_it_helps": "Leaving stray files can interfere with the evaluator's build (e.g., duplicate main functions, unexpected sources picked up by CMake) and keeps the submission clean.",
      "examples": [
        "rm -f scratch_main.cpp scratch_ref.cpp scratch_run scratch_ref; rm -rf .tmp; ls -la",
        "rm -rf .selftest && ls -a",
        "rm -rf _selftest _selftest.cpp _tmp && ls -la"
      ],
